import react from '../../../../snippets/react.tsx?raw'

`@familiar-ai/client` connects to the HTTP API, mirrors everything the event stream sends and derives a transcript a chat UI can render. Familiar's own web app is built on it.

```sh
npm install @familiar-ai/client
```

## The store

<Code code={client} lang="ts" title="client.ts" />

`createFamiliarStore<Api>(url, options)` opens the event stream straight away. `Api` is your host's API type, here the `Api` exported beside [`createHttpApi`](/familiar/build/serve-the-api/#choose-routes), imported with `import type` so no server code reaches the browser. It is required, and the store offers exactly the commands whose routes your host serves. The optional `fetch` makes every request, including stream reconnects, so you can attach a fresh credential each time. An open stream keeps the credentials it started with until it reconnects.

The store is read-only. You read it with `getState()` and `subscribe()`, and change things only by calling commands. State is grouped:

- `conversation`: the live `view`, older `history`, `loadOlder()`, and the commands `send`, `abort`, `modelOptions`, `setModel` and `setThinkingLevel`
- `transcript`: the derived chat items and whether a run is `busy`
- `memory`: streamed `facts` and `episodes`, with `revise`, `retire`, `setPinned` and `health`
- `schedules`: streamed `items`, with `cancel`
- `account`: the streamed sign-in `state` and its commands
- `push`, `connections` and `mcp`: commands only, present when the host serves any of them

Streamed documents are `undefined` until they arrive, and `null` when the server sends none.

`send(text)` posts a message with a fresh `requestId`. The host decides who sent it.

## The transcript

`state.transcript.items` is what a chat shows, in order. Each item has an `id` that stays the same across updates. Use it as the key.

- `message`: a person's words, with their `author`, and `queued` while it waits for the current run
- `reply`: Familiar's `text`, `thinking` and `toolCalls`, with `streaming`, `stopped` and any `error`
- `scheduled`: a schedule's prompt arriving, with its `due` time and `creator`
- `waiting`: a run has started but nothing is visible yet
- `compaction`: older messages were summarised for the model here

Each tool call has a `name`, `arguments`, `status` (`running`, `done` or `error`), text `output` and optional `details`. `details` is whatever the tool returned for UIs. Narrow it before you render it.

Older entries arrive through `conversation.loadOlder()`. `conversation.history.status` is `more`, `loading`, `failed` or `start`.

## The connection

`state.connection` moves through these values:

| Value          | Meaning                                                                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `connecting`   | The first stream request is under way                                          |
| `open`         | A compatible protocol handshake and full view have arrived                     |
| `reconnecting` | A network error, closed stream, 5xx or 429. The store retries with fresh state |
| `unauthorized` | The stream was answered 401 or 403. Retries stop                               |
| `failed`       | Any other unusable answer, such as a 404. Retries stop                         |
| `outdated`     | The protocol handshake was missing or incompatible. Retries stop               |

The store never reloads the page or signs anyone in. After a terminal state, sign-out or an identity change, call `disconnect()` and create a new store. Commands reject with the server's error and aren't retried. Commands already sent still settle after you disconnect.

## React

Install React 18 or 19, then use the separate `/react` entry:

<Code code={react} lang="tsx" title="App.tsx" />

Create the bindings and the store once, outside render, where your app manages connections. `createFamiliarBindings<Api>()` types the provider and hooks to the same host API as the store. The provider doesn't open or close it. `useFamiliar` compares selections with `Object.is`, so return stable values such as a single field or a command. The vanilla entry doesn't load React.

## Type the client to your host

The store's commands follow its host API type one operation at a time. A host that serves `memory: { health: true }` gets `memory.health()` but not `memory.revise()`, and one that serves no MCP routes has no `mcp` at all. The same works for routes you compose yourself:

<Code code={typed} lang="ts" title="frontend.ts" />

Export the host's type from a type-only module and keep it as the inferred Hono type rather than widening it to `Hono`. A host route must accept everything the client sends and keep its typed response, or the store's type is an error. This narrows TypeScript only. It doesn't remove handlers or enforce permissions. The repository's [typed host example](https://github.com/AidanZealley/familiar/tree/main/examples/typed-host) is compile-checked against the packages.
